[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance explains what `AGENTS.md` files are, where to place them, and what to put in them. An `AGENTS.md` file is the cross-vendor standard for providing an AI agent with persistent, repo-level context about how a codebase works — it is read autonomously by the agent at the start of every session, before any task spec arrives. It complements, but does not replace, the task-specific context assembled by the dispatch pipeline.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Reduces agent exploration time** — a well-authored `AGENTS.md` means agents spend fewer tokens on `grep`, `find`, and directory listing to understand the repo, and more on the task itself
- **Cross-vendor portability** — GitHub Copilot cloud agent, OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, and Google Jules all read `AGENTS.md` as a first-class input; one file works across all of them
- **Fewer broken builds in agent-produced PRs** — telling the agent which commands to run and which files to avoid eliminates the most common class of agent errors: touching the wrong files or running tests incorrectly
- **Aligns with industry practice** — `AGENTS.md` is the de-facto standard adopted by GitHub, OpenAI, and Anthropic as the repo memory bank for autonomous agents
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#relationship-to-existing-context-mechanisms]

### Relationship to Existing Context Mechanisms

`AGENTS.md` is one layer in a two-layer context architecture:

| Layer | Mechanism | Owned by | Scope | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Repo memory bank** | `AGENTS.md` (this document) | Platform/team | Persistent — applies to every agent session in the repo | Evolves with the repo |
| **Task context** | Structured spec + `configs/agents/*.yaml` (GUID-TECH-IMPL-002) | Pipeline | Per-execution — assembled at dispatch time for the specific task | One pipeline run |

The dispatch pipeline injects task-specific context (goal, acceptance criteria, constraints). `AGENTS.md` provides the persistent background that makes task context actionable — the agent knows where to look, how to build, and what conventions to follow before the task spec arrives.

page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#industry-context]

### Industry Context

Every major autonomous AI coding agent reads a repo-level instruction file at session start. The cross-vendor convergence point is `AGENTS.md`:

| Agent | File read natively |
|---|---|
| GitHub Copilot cloud agent | `AGENTS.md` (nearest in directory tree; `copilot-instructions.md` for chat) |
| OpenAI Codex | `AGENTS.md` (documented in their real-world case study: first 17 log entries read `AGENTS.md`) |
| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` (same concept; also reads `AGENTS.md` via cross-reference) |
| Google Jules | `.gemini/context.md` (equivalent concept) |

When Gainwell's dispatch pipeline invokes any of these agents, the agent will look for `AGENTS.md` in the repository root before reading the injected task context. If `AGENTS.md` is absent, the agent must explore the repo from scratch every time — consuming context window and producing more variable output.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#what-belongs-in-agentsmd-vs-elsewhere]

### What Belongs in `AGENTS.md` vs. Elsewhere

| Content type | Where it goes | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Repo structure overview, key directories | `AGENTS.md` | Persistent — doesn't change per task |
| How to build, run tests, lint | `AGENTS.md` | Persistent — the agent needs this on every run |
| Enterprise coding standards and conventions | `AGENTS.md` (brief) or `.ai/constraints.md` (full) | Brief summary in `AGENTS.md`; full list in `.ai/constraints.md` |
| Golden Path declaration and catalog reference | `.ai/context.yaml` (PTN-APP-GOV-002) | Machine-readable; the structured catalog integration is separate |
| Task goal, acceptance criteria, constraints | Structured spec in GitHub Issue (STD-GOV-AI-001) | Per-task; injected by pipeline at dispatch time |
| System prompt for the agent | `configs/agents/prompts/*.md` (GUID-TECH-IMPL-002) | Pipeline-controlled; not in `AGENTS.md` |
| PHI field declarations | `.ai/context.yaml` | Machine-readable; `AGENTS.md` references it, doesn't duplicate it |

---
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#what-agentsmd-must-contain]

### What `AGENTS.md` Must Contain

Every `AGENTS.md` in a Gainwell repository that operates an agent dispatch pipeline **must** include all five of the following sections:
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#1-repository-purpose-13-sentences]

#### 1. Repository Purpose (1–3 sentences)

What this repository does and which bounded context or business domain it belongs to. The agent needs to know whether it is operating in a HIPAA-scoped claims processor or a non-regulated internal tooling repo — the constraints differ materially.

```markdown
## Repository Purpose

The `claims-processor` service is a HIPAA-scoped Java microservice that adjudicates
pharmacy claims against plan eligibility rules. It is part of the Pharmacy Solutions
bounded context. PHI is present — see `.ai/context.yaml` for field declarations.
```
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#2-repository-structure-key-directories-only]

#### 2. Repository Structure (key directories only)

A concise map of where things are. Do not list every directory — list only the directories an agent is likely to need to navigate: source, tests, config, and any non-obvious locations.

```markdown
## Repository Structure

- `src/main/java/` — application source code
- `src/test/java/` — unit and integration tests
- `src/main/resources/openapi.yaml` — OpenAPI 3.1 spec (always update when adding endpoints)
- `iac/` — Terraform modules for this service's infrastructure
- `configs/agents/` — agent routing configuration (do not modify)
- `.ai/` — AI context files (do not modify; managed by platform tooling)
```
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#3-build-test-and-lint-commands]

#### 3. Build, Test, and Lint Commands

The exact commands to build, run tests, and lint. This is the most critical section — Thoughtworks research found that the inability to run tests is the primary cause of agent-produced PRs with failing builds. Agents will try to run these commands; give them the right ones.

Include:
- The exact command and its prerequisites
- Whether it requires internet access (if sandboxed agents are used)
- Common failure modes and their fixes
- Which commands to always run before committing

```markdown
## Build, Test, and Lint

**Prerequisites:** Java 21 (via `.java-version`), Maven 3.9+. No internet required after `mvn dependency:resolve`.

**Build:**
```bash
mvn clean package -DskipTests
```

**Run tests:**
```bash
mvn test
```
Always run tests before committing. If tests fail due to TestContainers requiring Docker, this is expected in sandboxed environments — note the failure and commit anyway; the CI pipeline will validate.

**Lint / format:**
```bash
mvn checkstyle:check
```
Checkstyle is enforced in CI. Fix all violations before committing.

**Run OpenAPI validation:**
```bash
mvn openapi:validate
```
Run this whenever the API contract changes.
```

#### 4. Key Conventions and Constraints Summary

A concise statement of the most important coding conventions. This is not the full constraints list — that is in `.ai/constraints.md`. This is the subset an agent needs to avoid the most common errors on the first try.

Limit this to 5–8 bullet points. More than 8 items are unlikely to be consistently followed by agents in current models (Thoughtworks research: larger context does not mean all instructions are followed).

```markdown
## Key Conventions

- **PHI**: Never log fields in `.ai/context.yaml#phi_fields`. Use `PiiRedactionSerializer`.
- **Secrets**: External Secrets Operator only. Never `@Value` for secrets.
- **Tests**: Every new class requires a corresponding unit test class. Integration tests in `src/test/java/integration/`.
- **API changes**: Update `src/main/resources/openapi.yaml` alongside code changes to endpoints.
- **Commit messages**: `<type>: <description> (#<issue>)` — types: feat, fix, refactor, test, chore.
- **No new dependencies** without updating `pom.xml` and checking the approved dependency list in `.ai/constraints.md`.

Full constraints: `.ai/constraints.md`
```
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#5-files-and-directories-to-avoid]

#### 5. Files and Directories to Avoid

Explicitly list files or directories the agent should not modify. Without this, agents will sometimes modify infrastructure-as-code files, generated files, or platform-managed context files.

```markdown
## Do Not Modify

- `configs/agents/` — pipeline-managed; changes here require platform team review
- `.ai/` — managed by platform tooling; update via `task utils:update-ai-context`
- `generated/` — generated code; modify the generator, not the output
- `iac/` — infrastructure changes require a separate `agent:infrastructure` task
- `.github/workflows/` — pipeline changes require platform team review
```
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#optional-sections]

### Optional Sections

These sections add value in larger or more complex repositories but are not mandatory:

- **Prerequisites**: Tools, SDK versions, environment variables that must be set before any command runs
- **Known Environment Issues**: Sandbox-specific limitations (e.g., "Docker not available in CI sandbox — skip TestContainers tests")
- **Useful Entry Points**: Key classes, main files, or modules that are frequently the starting point for changes
- **Related Repos or Services**: Upstream/downstream dependencies the agent should know about
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#length-and-style]

### Length and Style

- **Target length**: 100–200 lines. Shorter is better — context window real estate spent on `AGENTS.md` is not available for code.
- **Use code blocks** for all commands. Agents copy commands from code blocks more reliably than from prose.
- **Concrete over general**: "Run `mvn test`" is better than "run your test suite." "Use `PiiRedactionSerializer`" is better than "handle PHI carefully."
- **No aspirational statements**: Only include things the agent can act on. "We strive for high quality" adds no value.

---
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#directory-placement]

### Directory Placement

`AGENTS.md` files use directory-level scoping — the nearest file in the directory tree takes precedence. Use this to provide repo-wide context at the root and override it for subdirectories with different conventions.

```
repo-root/
├── AGENTS.md                    ← Root: applies to all agents in this repo
├── src/
│   └── (inherits root AGENTS.md)
├── iac/
│   └── AGENTS.md                ← Override: specific instructions for IaC agents
└── configs/agents/
    └── (no AGENTS.md — managed by pipeline)
```

**For most repositories:** A single root-level `AGENTS.md` is sufficient.

**For monorepos or repos with distinct sub-domains:** Add directory-level `AGENTS.md` files in subdirectories where the conventions differ meaningfully (e.g., a Python data pipeline alongside a Java service).
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#creating-agentsmd-for-the-first-time]

### Creating `AGENTS.md` for the First Time

The fastest way to create a correct initial `AGENTS.md` is to run the GitHub Copilot cloud agent's built-in onboarding task against your repository. From the [GitHub Copilot agents page](https://github.com/copilot/agents), select the repository and submit the following prompt:

```
Your task is to create an AGENTS.md file in the root of this repository. The file should
give an AI agent reading it for the first time everything it needs to work efficiently:
the repository purpose, key directory structure, exact build/test/lint commands (verified
by running them), coding conventions, and files/directories to avoid modifying.

Keep the file to 150 lines or fewer. Use code blocks for all commands.
Do not include aspirational statements — only actionable facts.
```

Review the generated draft carefully. Verify every command by running it. Correct any inaccuracies before merging the PR. The Copilot agent cannot verify all commands in sandbox environments — human verification is required.
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#keeping-agentsmd-current]

### Keeping `AGENTS.md` Current

`AGENTS.md` is a living document. It must be updated when:

- The build system changes (e.g., Maven → Gradle, npm → bun)
- New mandatory conventions are added (e.g., a new linter, a new required test category)
- A new directory structure is introduced that agents are likely to need to navigate
- A directory is added to the "do not modify" list

**Process:** Treat `AGENTS.md` changes like any other code change — branch, PR, review, merge. Outdated `AGENTS.md` files are worse than absent ones because they give the agent confident but incorrect information.

**Ownership:** The team or platform engineer who owns the repository is responsible for keeping `AGENTS.md` current. Add `AGENTS.md` to your team's Definition of Done for changes that affect build commands or directory structure.
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#relationship-to-configsagentsyaml]

### Relationship to `configs/agents/*.yaml`

The `configs/agents/*.yaml` files (GUID-TECH-IMPL-002) and `AGENTS.md` are complementary:

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Agent reads it **autonomously** at session start. Provides persistent repo context. Not pipeline-controlled. |
| `configs/agents/implementation-agent.yaml` | Pipeline reads it and **injects** listed context files into the agent invocation. Controls which additional files are added to the agent's context window. |

The `context_files` list in `*.yaml` should **not** duplicate `AGENTS.md` — the agent already reads it. The YAML config should list additional domain-specific standards documents that are only relevant to the specific agent type (e.g., API standards for the implementation agent, doc standards for the documentation agent).

Before this guidance was established, teams sometimes listed `.github/copilot-instructions.md` in `context_files` to achieve the same effect as `AGENTS.md`. That workaround is no longer needed — `AGENTS.md` at the repo root is the standard mechanism.

---
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#step-by-step-adding-agentsmd-to-an-existing-repository]

### Step-by-Step: Adding `AGENTS.md` to an Existing Repository

1. **Review the current agent config files.** Open `configs/agents/*.yaml` and note any `context_files` entries that describe repo structure or build commands. These are candidates to move into `AGENTS.md`.

2. **Draft `AGENTS.md`.** Use the five mandatory sections above. Run every command you write. Confirm the directory structure you describe matches the actual repo.

3. **Remove redundant context from YAML configs.** After `AGENTS.md` is in place, remove any `context_files` entries from `configs/agents/*.yaml` that duplicate what `AGENTS.md` now covers. Keep only files that contain domain-specific reference material (standards docs, API specs).

4. **Test with a real agent session.** Run one agent task after merging `AGENTS.md`. Check the agent's execution log — are there fewer exploratory grep and find commands in the early steps? Are commands run correctly? Refine based on what you observe.

5. **Add to Definition of Done.** Add "update `AGENTS.md` if build or structure changed" to your team's Definition of Done for any change that affects build commands, directory layout, or key conventions.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#signs-your-agentsmd-needs-improvement]

### Signs Your `AGENTS.md` Needs Improvement

| Symptom in agent PR | Likely `AGENTS.md` gap |
|---|---|
| Agent ran the wrong test command | Build/test section absent or incorrect |
| Agent modified files in `configs/agents/` or `.ai/` | "Do not modify" section absent |
| Agent created new dependencies without updating `pom.xml` | Dependency convention not mentioned |
| Agent's first 20+ log steps are `grep` and `find` | Repository structure section absent or too vague |
| Agent formatted code inconsistently | Lint command not specified |
| Agent did not update the OpenAPI spec alongside endpoint changes | API convention not in key conventions |
| Agent committed test SSN patterns as test data | PHI convention not mentioned |

---
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#example-1-java-hipaa-microservice]

### Example 1: Java HIPAA Microservice

```markdown
# AGENTS.md — claims-processor

## Repository Purpose

The `claims-processor` service adjudicates pharmacy claims against plan eligibility
rules for the Pharmacy Solutions domain. It is HIPAA-scoped. PHI fields are declared
in `.ai/context.yaml` — do not log them or include them in test fixtures.

## Repository Structure

- `src/main/java/com/gainwell/claims/` — application source
- `src/test/java/` — unit tests (mirror package structure)
- `src/test/java/integration/` — integration tests (require Docker)
- `src/main/resources/openapi.yaml` — OpenAPI spec (update with endpoint changes)
- `iac/` — Terraform for this service only (do not modify; use `agent:infrastructure` task)
- `.ai/` — AI context files (do not modify)
- `configs/agents/` — pipeline config (do not modify)

## Build, Test, and Lint

**Prerequisites:** Java 21 (`.java-version`), Maven 3.9+.

Build:
\`\`\`bash
mvn clean package -DskipTests
\`\`\`

Unit tests (no Docker required):
\`\`\`bash
mvn test -Dgroups=unit
\`\`\`

All tests (requires Docker for TestContainers):
\`\`\`bash
mvn test
\`\`\`

Lint:
\`\`\`bash
mvn checkstyle:check
\`\`\`

Always run `mvn checkstyle:check` before committing. CI will fail on violations.

## Key Conventions

- **PHI**: Never log `.ai/context.yaml#phi_fields`. Use `PiiRedactionSerializer` from `com.gainwell.security.logging`.
- **Secrets**: External Secrets Operator only — never `@Value` for secrets.
- **New endpoints**: Update `src/main/resources/openapi.yaml` alongside code.
- **Tests**: New classes require a paired test class. Use `@Tag("unit")` or `@Tag("integration")`.
- **Commits**: `<type>: <description> (#<issue>)` — types: feat, fix, refactor, test, chore.
- **Dependencies**: Do not add new Maven dependencies without checking `.ai/constraints.md` approved list.

Full constraints: `.ai/constraints.md`

## Do Not Modify

- `configs/agents/` — pipeline-managed
- `.ai/` — platform-managed (use `task utils:update-ai-context` to update)
- `generated/` — generated from OpenAPI spec; modify the spec, not the generated code
- `iac/` — infrastructure changes need a separate `agent:infrastructure` issue
```
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#example-2-directory-level-override-for-an-iac-subdirectory]

### Example 2: Directory-Level Override for an IaC Subdirectory

```markdown
# AGENTS.md — iac/

## Context Override

This directory contains Terraform modules. Standard `mvn` build commands do not apply here.
Only reach this directory when executing an `agent:infrastructure`-routed task.

## Build and Validate

\`\`\`bash
terraform fmt -recursive
terraform validate
\`\`\`

Run both before committing. CI runs `terraform plan` on all PRs.

## Key Conventions

- Module inputs defined in `variables.tf`, outputs in `outputs.tf`.
- Use `gainwell/hipaa-eks-module` from the private registry — never the public registry.
- Tag all resources with `var.tags` (passed from the root module).
- Sensitive outputs must use `sensitive = true`.

## Do Not Modify

- `iac/modules/shared/` — shared modules owned by platform engineering
```

page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#phi-and-sensitive-data]

### PHI and Sensitive Data

`AGENTS.md` must not contain PHI field values, actual credentials, customer identifiers, or non-public business data. It may reference that PHI fields exist and point to `.ai/context.yaml` for the enumeration. This is the same prohibition that applies to GitHub Issues under STD-GOV-AI-001.
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#version-control]

### Version Control

`AGENTS.md` is a first-class repository artifact. It must be:
- Committed to the repository's default branch
- Reviewed in pull requests like any other file
- Updated via PR when conventions change (not edited directly on the default branch)
page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-003-agents-md-authoring-guidance.md#security-review-trigger]

### Security Review Trigger

An `AGENTS.md` update that changes the "Do Not Modify" section, removes a PHI convention, or modifies build commands should be flagged for engineering lead review. These changes directly affect what agents will and will not do in the repository.
